item.title: Steelers’ TJ Watt Sends Strong Message Amid Browns Trash Talk
item.description: Stakes are always high whenever the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cleveland Browns meet , regardless of where both teams stand in the standings. The intense rivalry between the two sides is already a big reason why their meetings will always matter. But the upcoming Week 8 Steelers-Browns game at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh will have lots of extra spice in it. For one, the winner of that game will find itself leading the AFC North after eight weeks of football. Then there’s all the trash talk, which, along with the importance of the contest, Pittsburgh star edge rusher TJ Watt addressed on Friday . “We know how weighty this game is,” the former NFL Defensive Player of the Year Award winner said, via Ashley Wenskoski of Pittsburgh Sports Tonight. “I don’t hear any of that stuff,” Watt added about the smack talk coming from the Browns. “We know how weighty this game is.” TJ Watt asked ahead of facing the Browns how he reacts to trash talk from the opponent prior to the game “I don’t hear any of that stuff.” pic.twitter.com/ZDtOBHsyED — Ashley Wenskoski (@AshleyWenskTV) October 30, 2026 What Happened in The First 2026 Steelers-Browns Game Oct 11, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; A Pittsburgh Steelers helmet sits on the field before the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The Steelers and the Browns first met this season in a Week 4 showdown at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland. Pittsburgh entered that game coming off a close home win over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3, but failed to sustain its momentum, as the Browns came away with a 27-24 win. That game can also be best remembered for Browns kicker Andre Szmyt’s career-long 56-yard field goal that sealed the win for Cleveland. Aaron Rodgers went 22/30 for 299 passing yards and three touchdowns and two interceptions versus Cleveland, while also taking five sacks for a loss of 30 yards. He is looking for better protection in the pocket this time around, as the Steelers look to score their sixth win of the campaign. Watt had four total tackles with a sack, a pass defended and two quarterback hits in that game against the Browns. Oct 1, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker T.J. item.title: Lions’ Amon-Ra St. Brown Makes Eye-Opening Jared Goff Admission
item.description: Detroit Lions star wide receiver Amon-ra St. Brown recently shared something that seemingly surprises him about quarterback Jared Goff. St. Brown has been playing alongside Goff for years now , but he admitted that he doesn’t always realize the quarterback is under immense pressure when throwing the football. “Half the time I don’t even know he’s getting hit when he’s throwing it … and I realize the next day watching tape that he got blasted. He’s as tough as they come,” St. Brown told reporters on Friday via 97.1 The Ticket . Amon-Ra St. Brown on "one thing that's very underrated about Jared" "Half the time I don't even know he's getting hit when he's throwing it … and I realize the next day watching tape that he got blasted. He's as tough as they come." pic.twitter.com/IeYhNRmWiW — 97.1 The Ticket: (@971theticketxyt) October 30, 2026 Goff Has Been Steady in The Pocket For The Lions in 2026 Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detailed view of a Detroit Lions helmet at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images For what it’s worth, Goff has been fairly protected in the pocket in the 2026 NFL season, at least based on the fact that he’s in the middle of the road in terms of sacks absorbed, with 17. Cleveland Browns starting quarterback Deshaun Watson tops the list entering Week 8 with 25 sacks. Moreover, Goff has a 5.11 percent sack rate , below the league average of 6.3 percent. The 32-year-old Goff will look to keep it going for the Lions’ offense this coming Sunday, when Detroit looks to sustain its post-bye week momentum. The former No. 1 overall NFL draft pick has 1,788 passing yards and 14 touchdowns on a 67.3 percent pass completion rate. Goff is also yet to get picked, and he’ll try to keep it that way , as the Lions face an NFC North rival this weekend. Detroit will be the latest team to attempt to give the Minnesota Vikings their first loss of the season when they square off at Ford Field in Detroit for a Week 8 showdown. item.title: Ole Miss – Auburn OPEN thread
item.description: OXFORD, MISSISSIPPI - OCTOBER 17: Deuce Alexander #1 of the Mississippi Rebels enters the field before the game against the Missouri Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Oxford, Mississippi. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Maybe you are new to this rivalry if we want to call it that, and maybe rivalry is too strong of a word. But if you haven’t been around as long as some of the staffers of this blog, the Auburn game has been a sore spot on the schedule in the past. At one point, it was the Tommy Tuberville game where a former coach came back to raucous boo’s but who also almost always went home with the win. There has always been some friction with this program whether it be through some recruiting practices or the resurgence of their program via Cam Newton or the roller coaster nature of how high and low Auburn has been while Ole Miss experienced somewhat the same. Then there was the Laquon Treadwell game that truly was one of the more heartbreaking endings of an Ole Miss game that I have personally attended. No notes just absolutely terrible. Auburn has gotten the best of Ole Miss six of its last eight games in this series though the Rebels have won the last two. The last time the Rebels had a three game win streak against the Tigers dates way back to 1949-1952. YIKES. This year seems different though with these two teams not facing each other the past couple seasons. Ole Miss is clearly fighting for a playoff spot while Auburn is fighting for bowl eligibility. The Tigers have one of the best wins in the country with its upset over Georgia, but are they done with their spoiler status? You can reasonably look at the remainder of its schedule and see three wins (Arkansas, Miss. St. and Samford), which puts Auburn back in the bowl picture in the first year of the Alex Golesh era. An upset over Ole Miss or in the Iron Bowl would have the War Eagle faithful feeling very good about its future compared to the last few years. The Rebels though are coming off a hard fought loss to No. 11 Texas with a massive game next week against No. 3 Georgia. This is a trap game pure and simple for Pete Golding and his squad, and any missed assignments this week are going to sting for this fanbase that is already strongly questioning if the Rebels are who we thought they were supposed to be. Last week was also probably the worst game Trinidad Chambliss has had in a starting role under center. His Heisman hopes got a lot slimmer after facing one of the best defenses in the country, and now he needs to show out against Auburn. The Rebels do technically get to bowl eligibility with a win, but those days of hoping for a trip to Birmingham and Shreveport are long past this fanbase. Right now, it is a “take care of business” game in the Vaught. HYDR, cheers!

item.title: Cardinals Get Major Jeremiyah Love News Ahead of Cowboys Clash
item.description: Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love appears to be ready to go for Week 8 after missing some time. The rookie out of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish football program sat out the last two Arizona games with an ankle injury , but is expected to make his return to action this Sunday for a matchup against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in Arlington. According to Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur, Love will take the field versus the Cowboys, per Cardinals reporter Darren Urban . Love has been trending in the right direction toward his availability for the Dallas game this week. After missing three practices heading into Week 7’s game against the Denver Broncos, Cardinals Rookie RB Love Ready to Go For Cowboys Game Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love (4) warms up before their game against the Seattle Seahawks at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Sept. 20, 2026. Love was a limited practice participant on Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, he was upgraded to a full participant, a great indication of his chances to suit up to face the Cowboys on the road. Love’s ankle issue goes way into Week 2, and it could be something that he and the Cards will have to manage for the rest of the 2026 NFL season. In any case, he has the green light to play again, and Arizona could potentially see him have his breakout game as soon as Week 8’s Dallas tilt. The Cowboys have one of the most porous run defenses in the league, making them an ideal opponent to face for Love and Arizona’s rushing attack. Through seven weeks, the Cowboys are last in the league with 145.7 rushing yards allowed per game. The 21-year-old Love has rushed for 90 yards or more just once in the five games he’s played so far in the NFL. Overall, he enters Week 8 with only 245 rushing yards and a touchdown on 67 carries for an average of 3.7 yards per carry. Bam Knight led Arizona in rushing in the two games Love missed. item.title: Flick could field a new-look Barcelona midfield trident against Alaves – report
item.description: Flick could field a new-look Barcelona midfield trident against Alaves – report Gavi is reportedly in line to start for Barcelona against Deportivo Alaves , with Hansi Flick considering a midfield combination featuring the Spaniard alongside Pedri and Rodri. According to SPORT , the 22-year-old could receive an opportunity as Barcelona prepare for a demanding run of fixtures before the November international break. As expected, Flick will rotate his starting XI for the La Liga encounter, particularly with several first-team players unavailable and important matches against Aston Villa and Atletico Madrid approaching. Gavi’s potential inclusion would therefore offer the midfielder valuable playing time while allowing the manager to distribute minutes across his squad. Gavi could benefit from Barcelona’s midfield rotation Dani Olmo’s absence through injury has reduced Flick’s options, while Fermin Lopez may also need to be managed carefully given the schedule ahead. Gavi is likely to start against Alaves. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) Barcelona have confirmed that Olmo is expected to miss around a month after suffering an adductor injury. On that note, Gavi, who has only played 191 minutes this season, has consequently emerged as a candidate to start against Alaves. Although he has not been a regular member of the starting XI this season, his energy, pressing and ability to compete in midfield could make him a useful option for a fixture in which Barcelona are looking to respond positively, especially after consecutive defeats against PSG and Real Madrid. Pedri and Rodri could form a new midfield partnership If selected alongside Pedri and Rodri, Gavi would feature in a midfield trio that Flick has not previously started together this season. In fact, it would also mark the seventh different midfield combination used by the Barcelona manager during the campaign. Gavi has never started alongside Pedri and Rodri. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Rodri and Pedri have featured regularly with both Fermin and Olmo, while Gavi and Marc Bernal have generally had fewer opportunities from the beginning of matches. A new combination could give Flick a chance to assess another balance of technical quality, intensity and defensive work. Aston Villa and Atletico Madrid fixtures influence Flick’s decision Barcelona’s schedule provides a clear reason for rotation. The Catalans face Aston Villa in midweek before travelling to meet Atletico Madrid on November 8, making workload management an important consideration. Flick still has Frenkie de Jong, Bernal, Fermin and Brian Farinas available as midfield alternatives, although giving Gavi a start against Alaves would allow him to contribute without requiring the same players to shoulder the workload across every fixture.

item.title: Ed Oliver’s return can help unlock Bills defense
item.description: There has been much conversation around the defensive play of the Buffalo Bills this season and the shortcomings under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. While many Bills fans have been frustrated, myself included, there is one piece of the equation that has not been discussed enough this season. Thanks to multiple injuries, star defensive tackle Ed Oliver has only appeared in three games for Buffalo this season. Oliver missed week two after suffering a hip injury in warm-ups, and then excited the game early after taking a shot to his left knee during week 4. Much of the focus on the defense’s shortcoming have been centered around the play of the secondary and linebacker corps, I would argue that Oliver’s absence has had the greater impact. Statistically speaking, the Bills defense has performed at a higher level with Oliver on the field. The team has given up 25.3 points per game when Oliver plays, compared to 31.7 per game when he does not. The Bills also allow less yards per game when Oliver plays, and have 17 quarterback pressures during those games (as opposed to six total in the three games he missed). Looking past the statistics, it should also be noted that opposing offenses have marched down the field late in games to score late touchdowns in games that have been missed by Oliver (Los Angeles Rams, Las Vegas Raiders, and after exiting against the New England Patriots). If you want to take it one step further, Oliver’s absence seems to be having an adverse affect on the play of Greg Rousseau. In games played by Oliver, fans saw Rousseau tally four sacks to go along with six tackles for a loss. Without Oliver proves to be another story, where Rousseau did not have any tackles for loss in those games. There has also been an impact on Deone Walker as Oliver has missed time, with the second-year defensive tackle being double-teamed on 71% of defensive snaps. While much of the conversation has focused on the secondary, I am optimistic that the anticipated return of Oliver will provide a much needed jolt for the Bills defense on Sunday. Let’s hope that I am right as the Bills face a tough challenge against Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens.

item.title: As the trade deadline approaches, should Browns listen to Jared Verse offers?
item.description: This time during the NFL season, two things are the most topical: Game results each weekend and the looming NFL trade deadline. The Cleveland Browns have gotten off to a great start with a 5-2-0 record. Could a trade help this roster, or perhaps the Browns should sit tight and ride with what brought them. RELATED: VERSE UNAFRAID TO TALK DESPITE ZERO SACKS The NFL trade deadline is November 10. The league instituted a deadline for teams to prevent clubs from stacking rosters right before the playoffs and keep competitive balance towards the end of the season. This year’s trade deadline has generated a lot of interest in the defensive line. This market has already begun. The Indianapolis Colts traded DE DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers. The Tennessee Titans traded star DL Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears. The Browns’ pass rush is not getting quick pressure from the defensive ends this year and hasn’t been the same since the team traded away All-World pass rusher Myles Garrett. In that trade, Cleveland received Jared Verse, who had gone to two Pro Bowls in two seasons, and was voted the “NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year” when he came into the league in 2024. The idea was that Verse would fill in for Garrett, but not take his place. In just seven games, the Browns have 20 sacks collectively. Verse has zero. This is a guy who had 7.5 last year and 4.5 as a rookie. What exactly is wrong with Verse? Should the Browns coaching staff keep waiting for him to blow up the opposition during passing plays? Is there a scheme or fit issue? Or maybe, should Cleveland make him available before the trade deadline? Well-Versed For months since the Garrett trade, all we have heard is that Verse wasn’t going to fill Garrett’s shoes, but was an exceptional athlete and would provide a very good pass rush. item.title: Nuremberg's Chatzialexiou to join Frankfurt as head of sport
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Joti Chatzialexiou speaks during a DFB press conference. (is associated with: «Nuremberg's Chatzialexiou to join Frankfurt as head of sport») Sebastian Gollnow/dpa Joti Chatzialexiou is joining Bundesliga side Eintracht Frankfurt as head of sport, leaving the same role at second-division Nuremberg. The former German Football Federation functionary will move on February 1 and replaces Markus Krösche, the two clubs confirmed on Saturday. "It is important to me not to make the move immediately, but to work with my successor so that the club has a successful future," Chatzialexiou, who is of Greek heritage, said in a Nuremberg statement. "Frankfurt's offer is special as it is my home-town club. Otherwise, I would not have thought about leaving." Chatzialexiou is signing a contract until 2030 with the Eagles, who sit 14th in the Bundesliga. Nuremberg coach Miroslav Klose, appointed by Chatzialexiou in 2024, is sad to see his boss go with the side in third spot in the second-tier. "He was a close confidant," he told a news conference. "But ... I'm convinced the club will find a suitable replacement." Krösche, viewed by pundits as one of the top transfer gurus in the Bundesliga, had asked to be released by Frankfurt and has been linked in the media with a sporting director job at AC Milan.

item.title: Paige Spiranac Plays Golf as Princess Peach: “I Cannot Stop Thinking About My B***s Right Now”
item.description: Paige Spiranac took part in a costume round during Halloween, wearing a pink Princess Peach outfit with a crown and corset, and said it challenged her nerves more than her skills. “This is like exposure therapy times 100,” Spiranac commented on her YouTube channel. The golfer played solo in Florida, as no one agreed to join Spiranac in such an unusual round. “Hey everyone, it’s Paige, or should I say Peachy,” she said as the video opened. “I’m decked in my favorite color, and people say I don’t have any shame, and I’m feeling kind of shameful right now. But you know what? It’s Halloween. You know what they say about Halloween. You can’t say anything bad about me today.” Her strapless costume was quite distracting. “I am so distracted. I cannot stop thinking about my b***s right now,” Spiranac said. “When I put this outfit together, I honestly didn’t try it on until I just changed in the car. And I didn’t really think this one through.” During the game, Spiranac looked at herself between hits. “If you see me after every shot, look down. I’m just checking,” she said. “I am just checking.” As she mentioned in the video, Spiranac’s favorite character is Princess Peach. “Who doesn’t want to be a princess for a day? And pink is my favorite color. So, it just made so much sense,” she shared her thoughts about the character. Spiranac dressed up for Halloween 31 times in October over the past several years; however, she wore her costume on the course only once. “Not that really anything I wear is golf course appropriate, but I thought this was a fun one to break out,” the golfer noted. The month-long costume project helped Spiranac develop a love of cosplay, including characters like Cammy from Street Fighter, Velma from Scooby-Doo, Pamela Anderson from Baywatch, other superheroes, and even some Disney characters. item.title: Posibles alineaciones del Barça-Alavés
item.description: Posibles alineaciones del Barça-Alavés El Barça recibe al Deportivo Alavés con la necesidad de puntos y confianza ante las recientes derrotas del equipo El FC Barcelona recibe este sábado (21 h ) al Deportivo Alavés en el Spotify Camp Nou , en un duelo correspondiente a la undécima jornada liguera que se antoja vital para los intereses azulgranas. Tras sufrir dos derrotas consecutivas frente al PSG en la Champions League y el Real Madrid en el Clásico , el equipo dirigido por Hansi Flick necesita los tres puntos para asegurar su liderato . Actualmente, mantiene la primera plaza con tres unidades de margen y buscan así disipar las dudas. Flick: «Nos toca reflexionar sobre qué podemos hacer mejor, qué debemos mejorar y qué tenemos que hacer». Foto: FC Barcelona El principal quebradero de cabeza para el técnico alemán radica en la línea defensiva. En los últimos tres encuentros ha encajado un total de ocho goles . Las lesiones por otro lado también castigan duramente a la plantilla. Ahora mismo, a las ausencias de Andreas Christensen , Eric García y Jules Koundé (cuya participación es muy dudosa), se suma la de Xavi Espart , que estará siete semanas alejado de los terrenos de juego por un esguince de tobillo. En la parcela ofensiva, Dani Olmo y Roony Bardghji tampoco estarán disponibles . Ante este panorama, Flick se verá obligado a alinear una zaga totalmente inédita. Los últimos ensayos a puerta cerrada apuntan a una línea defensiva formada por Brian Fariñas , Pau Cubarsí , Frenkie de Jong y Joao Cancelo , resguardando la portería de Joan García . La apuesta por Fariñas es firme. En rueda de prensa, Flick alabó su «trabajo fantástico» y confirmó que merece la titularidad. Mandatory Credit: Mike Frey-Im… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jim Smith There is something rather amusing about watching Novak Djokovic, arguably the greatest returner in tennis history, repeatedly stand on the baseline and watch tennis balls fly past him. It wasn’t so much because Djokovic was playing poorly or because he forgot how to return; it was mostly because Jan-Lennard Struff was playing one of his crazy matches where he seemingly can’t do anything wrong. Their second-round encounter at the Swiss Indoors Basel produced an extraordinary 48 combined aces, with Struff hitting 27 and Djokovic contributing another 21. The German eventually won 6-7(4) 7-5 7-6(5) , ending the match, rather appropriately, with another ace. His 27th, and it was hardly an ordinary victory. Struff had lost all eight previous meetings against Djokovic, winning just one set across those encounters. Now, at 36, he had finally defeated the 24-time Grand Slam champion after two hours and 36 minutes of exceptional tennis. Not too long ago, we examined some of the most remarkable serving performances in tennis history in our piece on best-of-three-match ace records in the wake of the extraordinary match in Brussels. But the real story in Basel wasn’t the number of aces; it was how the conditions allowed Struff to challenge one of the greatest defensive and returning players ever, and how brilliantly he took advantage. Basel Is Turning Tennis Into a Serving Competition Indoor tennis generally provides favorable conditions for serving as there is no wind to interfere with ball tosses, no sunlight to complicate preparation, and relatively little environmental variation between points. When those conditions combine with a fast-playing court, the result can be devastating for returners, and Basel has offered plenty of evidence this week. Ben Shelton struck an extraordinary 44 aces in his opening-round victory over Aleksandar Kovacevic, who contributed another 13. That is 57 aces in one match, just 3 short of the record, which you can read all about in our piece on the topic . Neither player lost serve, and Shelton needed three tiebreaks to secure the victory. Then came Djokovic and Struff. Another 48 aces. Perhaps the most revealing statistic wasn’t Struff’s 27, but Djokovic’s 21. The Serbian has developed an increasingly effective serve as he has grown older, but he has never relied on it as much as the traditional giants of the sport. item.title: Lakers star Luka Doncic given ‘a lot like James Harden’ verdict by Channing Frye
item.description: Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images Former NBA player Channing Frye believes that Luka Doncic could end his career without a championship, while also comparing the Slovenian to James Harden. Having started the 2026-27 season, averaging 36.2 points, Doncic is once again set to have a big scoring year and will probably be a frontrunner for the MVP trophy. This is the first year, the Lakers will have Doncic leading the way without LeBron James, which is why there will be some pressure on him but there is belief that with the way the team are playing, they could make some noise in the Western Conference, especially given the fact that several teams have some injury concerns. While he has elevated his game and delivered big performances repeatedly throughout his career, the 27-year-old is yet to win his first NBA championship. However, Channing Frye believes it is difficult for Doncic to win a championship due to his usage rate. Channing Frye compares Luka Doncic to James Harden Doncic and Harden are both great scorers. With the ball in their hands, they can dominate against any opponents, but Frye believes that is not what leads to a championship. Harden has a stacked resume, but he has not yet secured a ring and often fails to perform in the playoffs. While Doncic has had big games in the playoffs as well, his defence lets him and his team down. “I love Luka, I just don’t think the way he plays basketball is going to win a championship, that’s it. I think Luka is a lot like James Harden, both of those guys games are amazing, but their usage rate is not equating to championships, who plays like that, who has played like that and won a championship?” Frye questioned on the Road Tripping Show’s Channing’s Mailbag segment. According to Basketball Reference, Doncic, at 36.41%, has the highest usage rate for any player in the playoffs in NBA history. James Harden ranks all the way down to 32nd in the postseason, but in the regular season he ranks second on the same list behind Russell Westbrook. Luka Doncic’s usage rate this season at 40.27% is the third most ever in regular season. Frye’s point has some relevance, as Harden and Doncic both need the ball to make a difference. They can make a difference on offence, but their poor defensive abilities pose a problem in the postseason. item.title: 'I'm 87 and I've finished 400 Parkruns'
item.description: David Carbert runs most weeks at the Humber Bridge Country Park event [BBC] An 87-year-old man who completed his 400th Parkrun on Saturday said he thinks running may have added years to his life. David Carbert joined the Humber Bridge Country Park event 10 years ago because he didn't want to sit at home doing nothing. Carbert, who said he was feeling "fairly fit and well", has no intention of stopping and hopes to reach his target of 500 Parkruns, when he'll be nearly 90. Helen Penn, the event's director, said: "We love him - he is an inspiration." Jamie and Helen Penn, directors of the Parkrun, with David Carbert [BBC] Carbert rises early each week to do some stretches first at home, and runs in all weathers unless there is deep snow or ice. He said he was full of trepidation when he went along for the first time, aged 77. "I didn't want to make a fool of myself, but everyone welcomed me. "You know it's one big happy family here." Carbert said he achieved his personal best running time of 28 minutes and 13 seconds aged 80, but now completes the 5km (3.1-mile) course in around 38 minutes. "I think it will have added years to my life. "Really, I didn't want to sit around at home vegetating." Tony Nicholson (right), David Carbert's neighbour, has run with him for years [BBC] Penn said Carbert was very dedicated. "I think he's only just getting going. He's brilliant!" she said. Tony Nicholson, who has run with Carbert for years, said he was his role model. "We have a sprint at the end and he always wins. "It really annoys me," he joked. Carbert was a bit out of breath when he had finished and was asked how he felt. "I'm a bit shattered at the moment, but I'll recover", he said. item.description: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Micah Parsons is finally nearing his return to the field as the Green Bay Packers’ star defender is expected to take part in practice next week. Many expected Parsons to have already returned to the action following his ACL tear last year, which ended his 2025 season early. However, the 27-year-old is heading into Week Eight still yet to even suit up for the Packers. Although it is a process that should not be rushed, Parsons has received more criticism than some other players due to his openness in expressing his opinions online. In recent days, the defender was criticised for suggesting the Kansas City Chiefs do not scare him. Veteran presenter and Dallas Cowboys fan Skip Bayless has now received some pushback from Stephen A. Smith following his comments on Parsons failing to recover quicker from his season-ending injury. What Skip Bayless said about Micah Parsons which frustrated Stephen A. Smith Parsons has proven a divisive figure through his podcast and the Packers are yet to really see a return on their investment due to his injury. However, Smith was not impressed with what Bayless had to say surrounding Parsons’ lengthy absence from the game. “Patrick Mahomes and Michael Parsons got hurt the very same day last season. Patrick vowed, “I’m going to have surgery the next day on Monday,” which he did. “I’m going to be back for the season opener,” which he was,” Bayless said on Smith’s YouTube channel. “Micah has been out for 320 days and counting, and it could go up to, I don’t know, 350 days. item.description: Casey McLean (left) has scored seven tries at this World Cup [Getty Images] New Zealand delivered a statement victory as they thrashed Fiji 78-0 to book their place in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals. The Kiwis established a 24-0 lead with four converted tries in the opening 13 minutes as Fiji - who pushed reigning champions Australia close a week ago - had no response on Australia's Gold Coast. Fiji conceded eight tries in the first half and five in a fiery second period, during which half-back Brandon Wakeham was sent off along with New Zealand winger Ronaldo Mulitalo. Centre Casey McLean claimed four tries, Keano Kini scored two and Jahrome Hughes, Dane Gagai, James Fisher-Harris, Mulitalo, Xavier Willison, Briton Nikora and Erin Clark also crossed for Stacey Jones' team. "Pretty special and pleased about how we went about our business," said New Zealand captain Fisher-Harris. "Fiji are a good team but I thought we played really well. It was a battle of the forwards." Fiji's woes were not confined to the scoreline, with captain Apisai Koroisau suffering a suspected broken jaw as he clashed heads with Joseph Tapine in the eighth minute. Semi Valemei, who impressed with a hat-trick of tries against the Kangaroos, also left the field with a head injury during the first half. Meanwhile, New Zealand will now face an anxious wait to discover if Mulitalo faces a tournament-ending ban for a high shot on Ronald Philitoga, which prompted a fracas involving Wakeham. However, in his post-match news conference Kiwis head coach Jones confirmed that star full-back Kalyn Ponga, who broke his arm in the tournament opener against Australia on 15 October, has trained this week and could be involved in their last-four match against either Samoa, Tonga or England. item.title: 5 Ravens to zero-in on vs. Bills
item.description: The Buffalo Bills are set to host the Baltimore Ravens this weekend in a tough matchup that could have playoff implications. Buffalo is vying for the No. 1 seed in the AFC, and they currently sit two games up in the loss column on the New England Patriots in the AFC East. Baltimore, on the other hand, is currently in fourth place in the AFC North, but at 4-3, they are firmly involved in the AFC playoff picture. While the Bills and the Ravens may not be divisional foes, they very well could find themselves fighting for seeding once January hits. A head-to-head victory not only helps Buffalo maintain their divisional lead, but it could also make a big difference in their playoff path. Baltimore isn’t a typical last-place team; they are far too talented to be taken lightly, and the Bills know they have a fight on their hands this week. If they want to earn a win this Sunday, they’ll need to account for these five avens to watch. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Lamar Jackson After missing the last three games with an ankle injury, Jackson is poised to return, and just in time for the Ravens. Baltimore is always dangerous, but with Jackson back, an already dangerous offense becomes a big challenge for a struggling Buffalo defense. The Bills have traditionally hemmed Jackson in fairly well, but with a new coordinator and a new scheme on the defensive side, there’s no way to know if that success will translate this year. So far, Buffalo’s defense has had next to no success, as they sit 30th in points allowed and 31st in yards allowed this season. If Jackson’s mobility is limited, it could limit his effectiveness, as he consistently makes huge plays with his legs. While Jackson is perfectly capable of beating teams from the pocket, Buffalo has to force him to stay there and make him do it for four quarters. WR Zay Flowers After signing a big extension this offseason, Baltimore’s top receiver has justified that deal with a huge start to the season. Flowers has 40 catches for 608 yards and three touchdowns on 53 targets. He can operate from the outside and from the slot. He has tremendous speed, he runs great routes, and he can attack the defense at every level. In short, he’s a nightmare for a struggling pass defense like Buffalo’s. Hell, he’s a tough cover for anyone . After watching Christian Benford travel with Brock Bowers last week, it wouldn’t surprise me at all to see him draw the same assignment for Flowers. Benford can use his size and length—he’s 6’1” with 31” or 32” long arms, depending on the source—to jam the 5’9” Flowers at the line. Physicality is going to be the name of the game this week, as giving Flowers a free release is a recipe for disaster. Limiting him and making Jackson look elsewhere will be a key part of the game plan on Sunday. He has fallen behind Denzel Dumfries and most recently, Federico Valverde in the pecking order, with coach Jose Mourinho preferring the Uruguayan international in the right-back position. This hasn’t gone down well with Trent, although Rodra notes that the Englishman is not ready to throw in the towel just yet. The right-back’s high salary package at the Santiago Bernabeu could also prove to be a problem for his suitors. That is why there is no immediate movement, with respect to Trent’s future. But things could get interesting if the defender continues to trail behind in the pecking order at Real Madrid.

item.title: ‘I got to get better’ – Luka Doncic speaks out after Lakers loss to Warriors
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Luka Doncic put the blame squarely on his own shoulders after the Lakers fell to the Warriors. Luka Doncic dropped 37 points alongside seven rebounds and five assists, but the personal stat sheet couldn’t mask an ugly Lakers meltdown. Los Angeles built a comfortable 25-point cushion before Stephen Curry caught fire, spearheading a ferocious Golden State comeback that turned into a 112-95 rout. The bitter loss came with an extra sting for Doncic on social media, too, as midway through the rally, Curry shook him with a crossover that sent Luka tumbling to the hardwood before splashing a clean step-back three, handing the internet its favorite highlight of the night. Luka Doncic’s honest assessment of Warriors loss After the game, Luka Doncic shouldered the blame himself, insisting a new-look Los Angeles Lakers roster just needs real minutes together to click. Noticeably absent from his postgame breakdown was any mention of Steph Curry sending him sprawling to the floor, as Luka kept all his focus strictly on his own shortcomings. He said: “I don’t know what it’s going to take. Obviously, reps, just playing these games. Warriors is a good example. They play hard defense. They shock a lot, so it was a good game for us. I mean, not good because we lost, but it’s good, I would say, to practice those things. “But I don’t know what it’s going to take. It’s going to take some time for sure. We got a lot of new guys, but I really like playing with these guys. So, you know, everybody can be better than this. We’re up 25-23. Me first. I got to be better. And we just got to, we lose together, we win together.” Luka did his job, carrying the load with 37 points, but he was essentially fighting Golden State all by himself. The Lakers got next to nothing once the starters sat, getting crushed 50-7 in bench points. And in a tight matchup, you simply cannot survive being outscored by 43 from the sidelines. item.title: Bayern Munich Ready to Pounce On Arsenal Captain Martin Ødegaard
item.description: Bayern Munich are ready to pounce on a move for Arsenal captain Martin Ødegaard according to a report from Sky Sports in Germany. The German giants have held a longstanding interest in the 27 year-old, and have maintained contact with his camp for several seasons according to reports. Ødegaard has a contract with the Gunners until 2028, and the north London side want to do everything to stop the Norwegian international entering into the last year of his contract. The board have held initial informal talks over an extension to keep him at the club. According to the story from Sky Germany, Arsenal would consider selling their captain next summer, but only in the extreme case that they cannot find an agreement on a long-term extension. Several European heavyweights have also enquired about his situation. Losing Ødegaard would pose a huge structural revamp for Arsenal and Arteta in the creative department, but the good news for the Gunners is that the 34-time Bundesliga champions are currently not prioritising a move despite his reported ‘openness.’ For Arsenal, there is huge admiration for their club captain and there is a full expectation that he will sign if the club and his entourage can come to an agreement. Arsenal initially signed Ødegaard from Real Madrid on loan from Real Madrid in January 2021, and then made his move permanent in August 2021 for a fee of £30million. Arsenal then made him club captain in July 2022 following the departure of Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang. Martin Ødegaard celebrates after his winning goal against Chelsea in September (IMAGO / Sportimage) Ødegaard has made 248 appearances for Arsenal in all competitions, scoring 46 goals and providing 47 assists. The Norwegian captained Arteta’s side to their first Premier League in 22 years, though endured a tough 2025/26 campaign, missing large parts of the season through an ankle injury that he picked up whilst on international duty with Norway. He only managed to score one goal and provide eight assists for Arsenal during the campaign. This season, the ‘old’ Ødegaard seems to have resurfaced. He has played the majority of the available minutes for Arsenal, featuring in 14 matches for The Gunners so far this season. He has scored four goals, including winners against Chelsea in the Premier League and Napoli in the Champions League. He has also provided a singular assist. According to TransferMarkt, Ødegaard has a transfer value of £67million, but in the unlikely event of selling their club captain, Arsenal would be hoping for a value that far exceeds this.
